summary: Repo already dissects 142 in OAI_METHOD_142.md (verdict NEGATIVE, promise 0/5: its auxiliary-prime derandomisation transfers only through bounded-index Frobenius layers, the index-2/BM layer is free, full index = B2) and HARDNESS_MAP.md A5/A6 + OAI_DUMP_IMPACT.md §2.1 (efficient ES ⇒ deterministic QNR; 003 alone already puts QNR/prime square roots in P). The concrete step: the only square-root code in the search engines (scripts/exf_engine.c:34, Type I f | p²+4c²d step) is Tonelli–Shanks with a deterministic least-QNR trial search (z=2,3,…), so no randomised step exists in practice; derandomisation is irrelevant to ES search and to existence.

Coppersmith/Lenstra/CHN 'divisors in residue classes' is analysed in BRAINSTORM/s3_lll_lenstra.md (upper bound ≤11 per Lenstra line, decision not existence, promise 0), gon_lll_relation_lattice.md (b1) and B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md row 8. I ran the item's exact step on the (★) line: the Coppersmith regime 4C ≥ (4Cp+1)^{1/4} is ⇔ uB ≲ p^{2/3}, Lenstra regime ⇔ uB ≲ p^{1/2}; among primes p≡1(4) ≤ 10^7 the Coppersmith-regime (★) sub-lottery fails at 131/293005 primes in [10^6,10^7] (0.04%; 0.2% in [10^5,10^6]; largest 9820897), Lenstra-regime fails at 0.47% — consistent with a θ² share of the (log p)² main term. Algorithmically the regime still spans ≍p^{2/3} values of C, so no polylog search and no existence mechanism; new only as a per-prime calibration of s3's per-certificate split.

Verified erdosproblems.com/298 = Bloom's theorem (positive upper density A ⇒ finite S ⊂ A with Σ1/n = 1). The repo already locates the density→pointwise gap: BRAINSTORM/addcomb_unit_fraction_density.md §3.1 (PROVED from Bloom's Prop 1: |S| ≥ N^{1−1/loglogN}/z, because the Fourier step needs many elements divisible by each prime power q | lcm(S) to equidistribute q-adically — impossible with 3 terms; §3.2 the k=3 local-cancellation shadow is exactly ET's parametrisation), z31_unit_fractions.md (c) (blocked by fixed target + 3 terms + polylog count), B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md §4.4 (ANALOGUE, NOT SHARP). The 'missing uniform lower bound' asked for is the term-count/equidistribution hypothesis, already identified.

Freedom quantified: (★) has 3 parameters (u,B,C), 1 equation, ≍(p/4)log p candidates of which ≍(3/(2π²))(log p)² succeed (FRONTIER §2.1–2.2) — free choice yields only polylog winners, whereas the proved side of the pair (a primitive root exists) rests on cyclicity with an exact positive count φ(p−1) ≍ p/loglog p. So the minimal pair is mis-aligned: ES's 'free base' is like the least-primitive-root problem in a polylog window (polylog only under GRH, Shoup), not like existence of a primitive root. This is already the repo's mechanism table B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md M1a/M2/M3/M4 (fixed-modulus character events, group action, freedom-of-choice) and z52_deep_thin_pointwise_opus.md rows 14–15 (least primitive root, Heath-Brown).

PROVED (one line, ultrametric): if v_ℓ(n) − v_ℓ(4) = k ≥ 1 then some denominator has v_ℓ ≥ k, since v_ℓ(Σ1/x_i) ≥ min v_ℓ(1/x_i); gives v₂(n)≥4 ⇒ 4|, v₂(n)≥5 ⇒ 8|, v₃(n)≥2 ⇒ 9|, 5|n ⇒ 5| — the necessity half of every observed failure set, trivially. For odd n the 2-adic count forces exactly two denominators ≡2 (4) and one odd; inside (★) this is C odd, v₂(uB)=1, and that sub-family alone fails at 513/34392 primes p≡1(4) in [10^5,10^6] (1.5%), so the variant data's 0 prime failures ≤10^5 use non-(★) solutions. The 'exactly' (sufficiency) half is a strengthened ES conjecture (EVIDENCE only), a positive-density sub-lottery with no new leverage.
